name.text: Calculating the Area Swept by a Windscreen Wiper

questiontext.text:
The shaded region in the diagram below represents the area swept out by a windscreen wiper on a flat windscreen. Calculate the area of the shaded region correct to \(3\,\text{decimal places}\).

[[jsxgraph]] var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-12, 12, 12, -12], axis: false, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, keepAspectRatio: true }); // Centre of rotation, now visible and labelled var O = brd.create('point', [-2, -2], { name: 'O', visible: true, size: 2, fixed: true, label: { offset: [-14, -12], fontSize: 16 } }); // Fixed DISPLAY radii (keeps the picture a sensible size regardless of the // true randomized R, which can range up to ~187 cm) var R_outer = 10; var R_inner = 6; // The angle is NOT decoupled: it uses the real randomized theta, // since the sector's shape is the one thing students can visually verify var angleDeg = {#theta#}; var angle = angleDeg * Math.PI / 180; // Outer sector var P = brd.create('point', [O.X() + R_outer, O.Y()], {visible: false}); var Q = brd.create('point', [O.X() + R_outer * Math.cos(angle), O.Y() + R_outer * Math.sin(angle)], {visible: false}); brd.create('sector', [O, P, Q], { fillOpacity: 0.2, strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: 'black' }); // Inner sector (cuts out the centre, leaving only the annular sector shaded) var Pin = brd.create('point', [O.X() + R_inner, O.Y()], {visible: false}); var Qin = brd.create('point', [O.X() + R_inner * Math.cos(angle), O.Y() + R_inner * Math.sin(angle)], {visible: false}); brd.create('sector', [O, Pin, Qin], { fillColor: 'white', fillOpacity: 1, strokeWidth: 0 }); // Hatching lines between inner and outer arcs for (var t = 0; t <= 1; t += 0.05) { (function (s) { var a = angle * s; var x1 = O.X() + R_inner * Math.cos(a), y1 = O.Y() + R_inner * Math.sin(a); var x2 = O.X() + R_outer * Math.cos(a), y2 = O.Y() + R_outer * Math.sin(a); brd.create('segment', [[x1, y1], [x2, y2]], { strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 1 }); })(t); } // Base line along the starting radius var baseEnd = brd.create('point', [O.X() + R_outer, O.Y()], {visible: false}); brd.create('segment', [O, baseEnd], {strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 2}); brd.create('text', [O.X() + R_outer / 2 - 1, O.Y() - 1, function() { return {#R#} + ' cm'; }]); // Angle marker showing theta brd.create('angle', [baseEnd, O, Q], { radius: 2, name: function() { return angleDeg + '°'; } }); // Wiper label, positioned along the bisector of the swept angle brd.create('text', [ function() { return O.X() + (R_inner + R_outer) / 2 * Math.cos(angle / 2); }, function() { return O.Y() + (R_inner + R_outer) / 2 * Math.sin(angle / 2) + 0.6; }, 'Wiper' ]); // Wiper length label brd.create('text', [ function() { return O.X() + (R_inner + 0.5) * Math.cos(angle / 2); }, function() { return O.Y() + (R_inner + 0.5) * Math.sin(angle / 2) - 0.8; }, function() { return {#Wiper#} + ' cm'; } ]); [[/jsxgraph]]

\(\text{Area of the region swept}=\)[[input:ans1]]\(\,\text{cm}^2\)[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution:

The shaded region represents the area swept out by the windscreen wiper. From the diagram:

  • Sector angle: \({@theta@}^\circ\)
  • Outer radius of the sweep: \({@R@}\,\text{cm}\)
  • Wiper length: \({@Wiper@}\,\text{cm}\)

Step 1: Find the inner radius \(r\).

\( \begin{align} r &= R - \text{Wiper length} \\ &= {@R@} - {@Wiper@} \\ &= {@r@}\,\text{cm} \end{align} \)

Step 2: Write the formula for the area of an annular sector.

\[ A = \frac{\theta}{360} \times \pi (R^2 - r^2) \]

Step 3: Substitute the values and compute the area.

\( \begin{align} A &= \frac{{@theta@}}{360} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left({@R@}^2 - {@r@}^2\right) \\ &= \frac{{@theta@}}{360} \times \frac{22}{7} \times \left({@R_sq@} - {@r_sq@}\right) \\ &= \frac{{@theta@}}{360} \times \frac{22}{7} \times {@Radius_difference@} \\ &= {@A_val@}\,\text{cm}^2 \end{align} \)

Rounded to \(3\) decimal places:

\(\text{Area of the region swept} \approx {@A_3dp@}\,\text{cm}^2\)

questionnote.text:
\(\text{The wiper Radius}={@Wiper@}\,\text{cm}\)

\(\text{The radius of the windscreen}={@R@}\,\text{cm}\)

\(\text{The area of the region swept}={@A_3sf@}\,\text{cm}^2\)
